'''Robert A. J. Matthews''' (born 23 September 1959), is a British physicist and science writer.

After graduating in [[physics]] at [[Corpus Christi College, Oxford|Corpus Christi College]], [[Oxford University]], in 1981, Matthews took up a dual career in science writing and academic research. He is currently science consultant and columnist for the science magazine ''[[BBC Focus]]'', a freelance columnist for ''[[The National (Abu Dhabi)|The National]]'' in [[Abu Dhabi]] and visiting professor in the Department of Mathematics, [[Aston University]]. He is also a Fellow of the [[Royal Statistical Society]], a Chartered Physicist and a Fellow of the [[Royal Astronomical Society]].

==Science journalism==
Matthews has held various specialist posts on national newspapers in the UK, including technology correspondent for ''[[The Times]]'' and science correspondent for ''[[The Sunday Telegraph]]''. In addition, he has written on a freelance basis for, among others, ''[[New Scientist]]'', ''[[The Economist]]'', ''[[The Financial Times]]'', ''[[Reader's Digest]]'' and ''[[The Spectator]]''.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.robertmatthews.org/mediaCV.html |title=Robert Matthews' media CV |access-date=2007-05-15 |archive-date=2007-07-12 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070712032347/http://www.robertmatthews.org/mediaCV.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> His professional awards include Feature Writer of the Year in 2000, by the [[Association of British Science Writers]].

==Academic research==
Matthews has published research in refereed journals on a wide variety of subjects ranging from [[Bayesian inference]] and [[probability]] to [[astronomy]], [[chaotic cryptology]]<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Matthews |first=Robert |date=1989-01-01 |title=ON THE DERIVATION OF A "CHAOTIC" ENCRYPTION ALGORITHM |url=https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/0161-118991863745 |journal=Cryptologia |volume=13 |pages=29–42 |language=EN |doi=10.1080/0161-118991863745|url-access=subscription }}</ref> and [[neural computing]].<ref>[https://scholar.google.co.uk/citations?user=Iu8W_G0AAAAJ&hl=en  Matthews's page on Google Scholar]</ref> He has also won awards for his research, including an [[Ig Nobel Prize]], awarded in 1996 for his paper ''Tumbling toast, Murphy's Law and the fundamental constants''.<ref>{{Cite journal |first1=Robert A. J. |last1=Matthews |title=Tumbling toast, Murphy's Law and the fundamental constants |journal=[[European Journal of Physics]] |volume=16 |issue=4 |pages=172–176 |date=1995 |doi=10.1088/0143-0807/16/4/005 |bibcode=1995EJPh...16..172M}}</ref><ref name=IgNobel>{{cite web |url=http://improbable.com/ig/ig-pastwinners.html#ig1996 |title=Winners of the Ig Nobel Prize |access-date=4 October 2009 |date=1996 |publisher=[[Improbable Research]] |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.-->}}</ref>
 
==Published works==
Matthews is the author of several [[popular science]] books, ''25 Big Ideas in Science'' (2005),<ref>{{cite book |first=Robert |last=Matthews |title=25 Big Ideas in Science |publisher=[[Oneworld Publications]] |date=2005 |isbn=978-1-851-68391-8 |oclc=61129937 |url=https://archive.org/details/25bigideasscienc0000matt }}</ref> ''Q&A: Cosmic Conundrums and Everyday Mysteries of Science'' (2005)<ref>{{cite book |first=Robert |last=Matthews |title=Q&A: Cosmic Conundrums and Everyday Mysteries of Science (Sunday Telegraph) |publisher=[[Oneworld Publications]] |date=2005 |isbn=978-1-851-68399-4 |oclc=63134341 |url=https://archive.org/details/qa00robe }}</ref> and ''Unravelling the Mind of God: Mysteries at the Frontiers of Science'' (London: Virgin 1992).<ref>{{cite book |first=Robert |last=Matthews |title=Unravelling the Mind of God: Mysteries at the Frontiers of Science |date=1992 |publisher=[[Virgin Publishing]] |location=London |isbn=978-1-852-27362-0 |oclc=28182916}}</ref>

In 2016, he published ''Chancing It: The laws of chance and what they can do for you'' (London: Profile Books).<ref>{{cite book |first=Robert |last=Matthews |title=Chancing It: The Laws of Chance and What They Can Do For You |date=2016 |publisher=[[Profile Books]] |location=London |isbn=978-1781250303}}</ref>
